people.name: Egeria

roles.t: Pilgrim in the Holy Land, Sinai, Egypt and Mesopotamia

people.summary: A woman from the far west of the empire, probably Gallaecia, whose letters to her 'sisters' at home describe a three-year pilgrimage to Jerusalem, Sinai, Egypt, Edessa and Constantinople. The surviving text (the Itinerarium Egeriae) is the fullest early account of the Jerusalem liturgy and an important witness to spoken Latin.

people.name: Melania the Younger

roles.t: Ascetic; founder of monasteries on the Mount of Olives

people.summary: Granddaughter of Melania the Elder and heiress to one of the largest fortunes in the Roman West, she and her husband Pinianus liquidated estates across Italy, Sicily, Africa, Spain and Britain from c. 405, left Rome before Alaric's sack, lived at Thagaste near Augustine, and settled in Jerusalem, where she founded monasteries on the Mount of Olives.

people.name: Germanus of Auxerre
people.summary: Former provincial official turned bishop of Auxerre, sent to Britain in 429 (and perhaps again c. 445) to combat Pelagianism. His Life by Constantius of Lyon credits him with the 'Alleluia victory' over Picts and Saxons, one of the few narrative glimpses of sub-Roman Britain. He died at Ravenna while interceding for the rebel Armoricans.
